proposed_strategy: For a_n=1-1/n (n>=2), 1-|a_n|=1/n gives harmonic divergence and rules out every nonzero H^p realization by the Blaschke necessary condition. On a nonempty compact K in the disc with rho=max_K|z|<1, the factor modulus identity yields 1-|b_{a_n}(z)| >= (1-rho^2)/(8n), uniformly on K. Thus the normal-convergence deviation sum diverges, while |B_N(z)| <= exp[-(1-rho^2)/8 sum_{n=2}^N 1/n] (and any prescribed factor zero makes the product zero) proves locally uniform convergence of the partial products to zero. For the holomorphic witness, a_n in K implies n<=1/(1-rho), so the prescribed support is compactly finite; apply the corrected plane-domain zero-divisor theorem with multiplicity one to obtain a nonzero holomorphic function with exactly these simple zeros, which lies in no H^p.
